subject: Build-to-close MAP: acceptance gates & test playlist
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthndx.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@healthndx.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP inputs — success criteria & acceptance tests

Hi Rachel / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput and the accuracy on the sample dataset. We want to formalize a short MAP so internal stakeholders (data science, infra, procurement) have a clear path to close. High-level asks below:

- Acceptance objectives:
  - Functional: model-level accuracy on our clinical-normalized QA set >= 92% (macro F1).
  - Latency: p95 end-to-end < 350ms for single-turn requests; p95 < 250ms for cached prefix paths.
  - Stability: 99.5% request success rate during 2-hour soak at expected concurrency.
  - Data controls: confirm retention / deletion window and KMS integration for keys.

- Exit gates we need in MAP:
  1) Security & compliance checklist completed (SOC2 artifacts + encryption proof).
  2) Performance verification pass on our benchmark harness.
  3) SOW + licensing approved by procurement/legal.

- Acceptance tests we care about (examples):
  - Smoke: basic inference on 50 production-like prompts (pass rate >= 95%).
  - Regression: targeted correctness tests where outputs must match golden responses > 90%.
  - Robustness: adversarial prompts and sanitization checks.

I've attached a short one-pager with our evaluation constraints (HealthNDX-eval-requirements.pdf). Procurement is looped on this thread — they said legal review will take ~7 business days once we submit SOW. Can you send a MAP draft and proposed timeline (2–3 week eval preferred) — include rollback triggers and canary plan.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director of Data & Analytics
HealthNDX

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthndx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP inputs — success criteria & acceptance tests

Elena — thank you, this is super helpful and clear.

Attached is a draft MAP (MAP-draft-v0.1.xlsx) that maps your exit gates to concrete tests and owners. Highlights:

- Proposed cadence (two-week sprint cadence):
  - Week 0 (kickoff): env provisioning, test data ingest, security scoping.
  - Week 1: smoke & regression; first performance pass.
  - Week 2: soak, canary, and handoff runbook; procurement/Legal sign-off parallel track.

- Key acceptance artifacts:
  - Smoke test report (pass/fail per prompt) — owner: Redwood QA (Karthik).
  - Performance deck (p50/p95/p99 under defined load) — owner: Redwood SRE (Marissa).
  - Security evidence bundle (SOC2 artifact pointers, KMS config screenshots) — owner: Redwood Security.

- Rollback triggers we propose to include in MAP:
  - Any regression causing >5% drop vs baseline accuracy on golden set.
  - Sustained p95 latency > 400ms in production canary for >15 minutes.
  - Any data-exfiltration finding from security review.

Quick asks: can you confirm the canonical golden test set (we want the file and an expected scoring script) and a preferred 2-hour window for the soak run? We can push a draft SOW (SOW-draft.pdf) once procurement confirms billing terms.

I'll set up a short sync for Friday to walk through the MAP columns and owners — does 10am PT work?

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthndx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP inputs — success criteria & acceptance tests

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 11:03 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Elena — thank you, this is super helpful and clear.

Adding the technical test scaffold so we have deterministic pass/fail checks. Below are the tests I plan to run and the minimal pass criteria; I'll attach the runbook (smoke-test-scripts.md) to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d5E6fMAPs

- Functional / Regression suite:
  - 200 golden prompts across intents; pass if macro-F1 >= 92% and no category drops > 6%.
  - Exact-match checks for templated responses (e.g., medication extraction) 95%+.

- Performance / Load tests (test harness using k6 + Redwood perf runner):
  - Baseline: single-client p95 <= 220ms (warm cache).
  - Soak: 50 RPS sustained for 2 hours: end-to-end p95 <= 350ms, error rate < 0.5%.
  - Canary traffic: ramp 0 -> 10% traffic: monitor p95 and error spikes, auto-fallback to baseline model on defined thresholds.

- Resource & cost observations:
  - Capture GPU utilization and token cost metrics; estimate cost per 1k effective tokens for forecast.

Implementation notes / fallbacks:
- We'll run quantized model variant for cost test; if accuracy drop >3% vs FP16 on golden set, document as explicit tradeoff and do not promote to canary.
- For deterministic scoring we will check both macro/n-gram overlaps and a domain-weighted scoring script (will upload).

Cc'ing Marissa to own the soak/perf verification and ensure the perf deck templates are ready.

—Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthndx.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@healthndx.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP inputs — success criteria & acceptance tests

Thanks — this looks good and practical. A few procurement / legal constraints to flag before we finalize MAP and SOW:

- Legal will require a 30-day notice on any data export changes; include that as a constraint in the MAP.
- We need the canary to run in our VPC with customer-controlled KMS for encryption-at-rest. Please confirm the onboarding steps for private deployments.
- Procurement: billing contact is procurement@healthndx.com. We will queue the SOW once we get the draft and a high-level pricing estimate (monthly committed and burst rates).

Timelines:
- We can commit to the two-week MAP timeline but legal says SOW turnaround will be 7 business days, so earliest commercial sign-off is Week 3. That is acceptable if the technical MAP runs in Week 1–2 and canary + handoff in Week 3.

Please include explicit rollback steps in the MAP (we want runbook snippets like: traffic cut to 0% -> redeploy previous container -> validate golden set smoke tests pass before full restore). Also include a short acceptance checklist to hand to our PM and Security reviewer.

If you can send the updated MAP and SOW draft by Monday EOD, procurement will prioritize review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we should be ready to schedule the Friday walkthrough you proposed. 10am PT works for my team.

Best,
Elena
Director of Data & Analytics
HealthNDX
